sentences.latin: Magister puerum et puellam vocat.
sentences.english: The teacher calls the boy and the girl.

sentences.latin: Puer librum magnum portat.
sentences.english: The boy carries a large book.

sentences.latin: Puella mensam parvam videt.
sentences.english: The girl sees a small table.

sentences.latin: Magister verba clara dicit.
sentences.english: The teacher says clear words.

sentences.latin: Itaque verba magistri audiuntur.
sentences.english: And so the teacher's words are heard.

sentences.latin: Magister puellae librum novum dat.
sentences.english: The teacher gives the girl a new book.

sentences.latin: Puella hunc librum aperit.
sentences.english: The girl opens this book.

sentences.latin: Puer verba longa scribit.
sentences.english: The boy writes long words.

sentences.latin: Sed puer verbum difficile quaerit.
sentences.english: But the boy seeks a difficult word.

sentences.latin: Magister puerum monet et puellam laudat.
sentences.english: The teacher advises the boy and praises the girl.

sentences.latin: Nauta fidelis iter longum et difficile parat.
sentences.english: The loyal sailor prepares a long and difficult journey.

sentences.latin: Nauta stellas claras et lunam candidam videt.
sentences.english: The sailor sees the bright stars and the radiant moon.

sentences.latin: Nauta periculo maris magni terretur.
sentences.english: The sailor is frightened by the danger of the great sea.

sentences.latin: Sed nauta fortis insulam parvam et pulchram petit.
sentences.english: But the brave sailor makes for a small and beautiful island.

sentences.latin: Nauta amico suo piscem magnum dat.
sentences.english: The sailor gives his own friend a large fish.

sentences.latin: Amicus aquam dulcem et cibum bonum portat.
sentences.english: The friend carries sweet water and good food.

sentences.latin: Nauta amicum suum de periculo monet.
sentences.english: The sailor warns his own friend about the danger.

sentences.latin: Amicus verba nautae audit et respondet.
sentences.english: The friend hears the sailor's words and replies.

sentences.latin: Itaque nauta amicum ad mare ducit.
sentences.english: And so the sailor leads the friend to the sea.

sentences.latin: Iter longum finitur et nauta laudatur.
sentences.english: The long journey is finished and the sailor is praised.

sentences.latin: Femina sapiens et fidelis oraculum dei immortalis quaerit.
sentences.english: The wise and loyal woman seeks the oracle of the immortal god.

sentences.latin: In templo vetere vox clara numinis sancti auditur.
sentences.english: In the old temple the clear voice of the holy deity is heard.

sentences.latin: Ea vox periculum et mortem omnis populi dicit.
sentences.english: That voice tells of the danger and the death of the whole people.

sentences.latin: Femina misera verbis gravibus illius numinis terretur.
sentences.english: The wretched woman is frightened by the grave words of that deity.

sentences.latin: Sed omnis populus urbis nostrae a numine immortali servatur.
sentences.english: But the whole people of our city is saved by the immortal deity.
